newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Oct 8.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on Oct. 8:

WASHINGTON - Federal investigators are trying to determine whether hundreds of thousands of dollars in donations by the D.C. lottery board to local community organizations were handed out for political reasons.

LOUISVILLE - A group of 10 uncommitted voters who gathered to watch the presidential debate were still uncertain about President Clinton's character and Republican Bob Dole's vision after the 90-minute session.
WASHINGTON - A loss of discretion imposed by the U.S. Sentencing Guidelines fuels frustration among federal judges.

WASHINGTON - Compared with many other federal anti-pollution programmes, the Toxic Release Inventory is a low-budget, low-glamour item about which President Clinton and challenger Bob Dole fundamentally disagree.
WASHINGTON - A new variety of corn has reignited debate over the safety of genetically engineered foods and threatens to trigger a trade dispute between the United States and the European Union.

JURMALA, Latvia - A retired typesetter from Takoma Park and his Latvian-American siblings should be able to reclaim their family's seaside estate lost to upheaval and war but the building happens to be the home of the Russian ambassador.
